_comment: Keyword pipeline for Howard Wedding Rentals. Sorted by priority_score DESC. Status lifecycle: queued -> in_progress -> published (or skipped). A 'skipped' entry MUST carry skip_reason and skipped_date so triage does not resurface it; skipped entries are permanent rulings, not deferrals.

queue.search_intent: informational/commercial — bride in the early stages of wedding planning searching broadly for what a seating chart is and how to build one, before she has settled on a specific tool or display format
queue.suggested_angle: Top-of-funnel pillar guide explaining what a wedding seating chart is, why couples need one, and how to choose between a DIY digital tool and a custom-printed display board — links out to the free seating chart tool and the foam board product without duplicating the existing step-by-step how-to or template articles

queue.search_intent: commercial — bride shopping for wedding table numbers, comparing styles and figuring out how they fit with her place cards and seating chart
queue.suggested_angle: Guide to choosing and ordering wedding table numbers — styles, sizing, materials — positioned as the natural companion purchase to custom place cards and a printed seating chart board

queue.search_intent: local/transactional — shopper looking to buy raw foam board sheets at a nearby store; not wedding-specific despite matching the guardrail term
queue.suggested_angle: Would need to pivot hard toward wedding seating chart displays specifically to avoid ranking for general craft-supply searches unrelated to our audience
queue.skip_reason: SERP mismatch — top results are entirely home-improvement/craft retailers (Home Depot, Dollar Tree, Menards, Michaels, Walmart) selling raw foam board sheets with local_pack intent, not wedding seating chart displays. This keyword only passed the automated guardrail because 'foam board' is a substring inclusion term; the real search intent is a crafter/DIYer buying raw material locally, not a bride. Publishing here would target the wrong audience.

queue.search_intent: mixed/ambiguous — majority intent is for Lucy Foley's novel 'The Guest List,' not wedding planning; unsuitable despite passing the guardrail substring match on 'guest list'
queue.suggested_angle: Not viable as written — would need a much more specific long-tail variant like 'wedding guest list to seating chart' to escape the novel's SERP dominance
queue.skip_reason: SERP mismatch — results are dominated by Lucy Foley's novel 'The Guest List' (Goodreads, Wikipedia, Reddit book club, Audible) plus generic dictionary definitions; virtually no wedding-planning content appears in the top 10. The bare keyword's actual search intent is the book, not wedding guest list management.

queue.search_intent: informational/commercial — bride wants a seating chart she can print herself, weighing a downloadable template against a professionally printed display board
queue.suggested_angle: Compares free printable seating chart templates against ordering a ready-to-display printed foam board — covering paper stock, sizing, and mounting for the DIY route, then the case for skipping that work with a custom board; distinct from the existing free-template roundup by focusing on the print-and-display step rather than the template download itself

queue.search_intent: informational/commercial — searcher comparing seating chart template formats and tools, with mixed wedding and non-wedding (classroom) intent
queue.suggested_angle: Would need to be folded into the existing wedding-seating-chart-template article as a 'which format should you use' section rather than published as a standalone post
queue.skip_reason: cannibalization — overlaps directly with the published wedding-seating-chart-template article (free templates, downloads, printables), and the SERP for this variant skews toward generic/classroom template tools (template.net classroom, weareteachers) rather than wedding-specific results. Not enough differentiation to justify a second standalone article.

queue.search_intent: informational — bride organizing her wedding seating table-by-table, looking for layout and display ideas for a table-based seating chart
queue.suggested_angle: Focused how-to for building a table-by-table wedding seating chart — numbering tables, grouping guests, and laying it out — before pointing to the printed foam board display as the finishing step

queue.keyword: how to make a seating chart
queue.search_intent: informational — same searcher intent as the published 'how to make a wedding seating chart' guide, just missing the word 'wedding'
queue.suggested_angle: Redundant with the existing how-to-make-a-wedding-seating-chart article; consider using this as an alternate title/meta-description variant on that page instead of a new post
queue.skip_reason: cannibalization — near-duplicate of the published how-to-make-a-wedding-seating-chart article. SERP for this bare variant is still dominated by wedding content (Canva, Brides.com, wedding floor-plan blogs), confirming identical search intent to the keyword already targeted (how to make a WEDDING seating chart). Publishing a second version would split ranking signals.

queue.search_intent: informational — generic reference lookup for foam board dimensions, not wedding-specific
queue.suggested_angle: Not viable as written — a genuine wedding angle would need to be something like 'what size foam board for a wedding seating chart' instead of the generic dimension lookup
queue.skip_reason: SERP mismatch — results are generic craft/print-supply reference content (Dollar Tree, print shops, foamboards.com) with no wedding relevance. Same false-positive pattern as foam-board-near-me: the guardrail substring match on 'foam board' pulled in a non-wedding craft-material query.

queue.keyword: where to print place cards for wedding
queue.search_intent: local/transactional — bride has already designed her place cards and is searching for where to get them printed, comparing local print shops, drugstores, and online/custom services
queue.suggested_angle: Compares local print shop, drugstore, and online options for printing wedding place cards, then makes the case for ordering custom-printed cards directly instead of DIY printing at home

queue.search_intent: informational — searcher wants to understand what church pews are; top-of-funnel opportunity to introduce church pew rental services for weddings
queue.suggested_angle: Definitive guide to church pews — what they are, their history, and how couples can rent authentic solid hardwood pews for their ceremony instead of standard folding chairs

queue.search_intent: commercial — bride shopping for name tags or place cards to help guests identify themselves at the reception
queue.suggested_angle: Clarify the difference between wedding name tags and place cards — when each makes sense, what guests actually prefer, and how to order printed place cards that double as keepsakes

queue.keyword: wedding place cards with meal choice
queue.parent_topic: wedding place cards with meal choice
queue.search_intent: transactional — bride planning a plated dinner needs place cards that clearly indicate each guest's meal selection to the caterer
queue.suggested_angle: How to create wedding place cards that show each guest's meal selection — design tips, what to print, how caterers use them, and ordering options including custom printed cards

queue.search_intent: navigational/transactional — bride wants a free online tool to build her wedding seating chart without paying for software
queue.suggested_angle: Roundup of the best free seating chart maker tools — compare Canva, SeatPlan, and other options, then explain why Howard's drag-and-drop tool is purpose-built for weddings (not classrooms)

queue.search_intent: commercial — shopper (likely a bride or event planner) looking to buy place cards for a seated dinner table setting
queue.suggested_angle: What to know before buying place cards for wedding tables — sizes, fold styles, printing options, and why custom printed cards are worth the upgrade over blank card stock
queue.skip_reason: cannibalization — the suggested angle (sizes, fold styles, printing options, what to order) is already the substance of the published article wedding-place-cards-guide. Publishing it would split intent signals between two of our own pages. Better folded into that article as a new section.

queue.search_intent: informational — bride planning her ceremony seating arrangement and looking for a visual template to share with her venue coordinator
queue.suggested_angle: Free wedding ceremony chair layout guide — standard row configurations, how many chairs per row, pew vs. chair comparisons, and a printable template to review with your venue
queue.skip_reason: traffic floor — volume 100 and traffic_potential 100 are both at the phase-1 minimum, so ranking it would not measurably move traffic. Still worth writing later as a conversion asset for the pew rental service (KD 3, highest-margin pillar), but not as a traffic play.

queue.keyword: how much does a church pew weigh
queue.search_intent: informational — bride or venue coordinator planning ceremony logistics wants to know if a pew can be moved/handled without professional help
cluster_siblings: how heavy is a church pew
queue.suggested_angle: Answer the literal weight question, explain what changes it (wood type, length, construction), then connect the weight to why delivery/setup/teardown should be handled by a rental service instead of DIY
